cases.exposure_context_quote: A twenty-seven-year-old male presented to the Emergency Room (ER) with the alleged history of ingestion of an unknown poison, amount unknown, ten hours back following a family dispute.
cases.agent_quote: An empty bottle of the pesticide amitraz 12.5% recovered from the patient’s room was brought along by the patient’s relative to which the patient agreed having ingested two teaspoonful of it.
cases.circumstance: suicidal ingestion following a family dispute

symptoms.quote: The patient immediately had two episodes of vomiting and then gradually developed altered sensorium in the form of drowsiness within two hours of ingestion of the poison.
gradually developed altered sensorium in the form of drowsiness within two hours of ingestion of the poison
the patient had a Glasgow coma scale score of 9/15 (E2V2M5)
Vital signs revealed a radial pulse of 50 beats per minute, blood pressure 90/50mm Hg
oxygen saturation of 86% in room air
His pupils were constricted bilaterally and sluggishly reacting to light.

cases.time_to_care: presented to ER ten hours after ingestion

labs.name: full blood count, renal function tests, random blood sugar, liver function tests, coagulation profile
labs.quote: His investigations comprising a full blood count, renal function tests, a random blood sugar level, liver function tests, and a coagulation profile were all within normal limits.

labs.name: arterial blood gas
labs.quote: Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis did not reveal any abnormalities

labs.name: serum cholinesterase
labs.quote: a serum cholinesterase level was within normal limit.

treatment.name: oxygen 2 L/min via nasal cannula
treatment.quote: The patient was provided oxygen at two litres per minute via nasal cannula, his oxygen saturation improved to 96%.

treatment.name: intravenous fluid bolus (500 ml 0.9% normal saline)
treatment.quote: He was managed by administering immediately a bolus dose of 500ml of 0.9% of normal saline

treatment.name: intravenous atropine 0.6 mg
treatment.quote: an intravenous dose of atropine 0.6mg following which his heart rate increased to 96 beats per minute

treatment.name: supportive management and monitoring
treatment.quote: Six hours of close monitoring with continuous supportive management resulted in the patient opening his eyes spontaneously with a purposeful response to verbal stimuli.

cases.outcome: complete recovery; discharged on fourth day in good health
cases.outcome_quote: He was finally discharged from the hospital on the fourth day in good health.
cases.notes: GCS improved to 15/15; symptoms resolved over next 12 hours; no hyperglycemia; no inotropic support required.
